text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nairobi University and Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology close indefinitely following riots by students mourning the death of their colleagues on Monday.
- The Roman Catholic Church in Kenya demands for the immediate start of the constitutional reform process.
- Twenty-two foreign missions express their indignation and criticism against police brutality against the public on Monday and urge the government to initiate dialogue urgently.
- The High Court dismisses with costs a lawsuit filed by 26 legislators from Nyanza province in western Kenya seeking the nullification of the just-ended voter registration exercise.
- Controversial Islamic preacher Sheikh Khalid Balala is due to arrive in Kenya on Saturday. He says he will sue the Kenyan government for forcing him into exile.
- Opposition leader James Orengo gives a formal notice to parliament to move a motion to pass a vote of no confidence in the government for failing to institute constitutional reforms.
- Parliament resolves to revive the Kenya Civil Servants Union which was disbanded 17 years ago.
- Police spokesman Peter Kimanthi says the force does not play a partisan role in discharging its lawful duties.
